title: Comparing EDI Compliance Requirements by Retailer
summary: EDI compliance requirements differ by retailer. Compare onboarding, ASN timing, penalties, and where each rulebook lives, with sources and dates.
body_markdown:
In this article, learn about:


-


How retailers start the compliance clock at different points


-


What each retailer counts as an on-time and accurate advance ship notice (ASN)


-


How Kroger and Target price electronic data interchange (EDI) violations in different units


Each retailer has its own definition of EDI compliance, even though the core documents are shared. The EDI 856 ASN and the[EDI 997 functional acknowledgment](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/articles/edi-documents-transactions) appear in the Kroger and Walmart rules alike. The clock, the ASN standard, and the penalty still belong to each retailer.


It is important to read every figure below with its date, since the retailers you sell to revise their policies on their own schedules.


## What Does “EDI Compliant” Mean at Each Retailer?


EDI compliant means meeting a separate rule set for each retailer, such as Kroger’s 90-day window or Target’s per-carton rate. The table below compares four retailers:


**Retailer**


**Onboarding Path**


**ASN Timing**


**Penalty Mechanics**


**Where the Rulebook Lives**


Kroger


Production first for the Food and Peyton groups, with no purchase order (PO) testing ([Kroger’s EDI terms](https://edi.kroger.com/EDIPortal/EDITermsAndCondition.html) )


ASN arrives before the product is received


1% of invoice value or $250, whichever is greater, after a 90-day window for distribution center purchase orders


Kroger’s public EDI portal


Target


Vendors accept Target’s Rules of Use for Partners Online, and Target requires an EDI system to receive purchase orders


Error-free EDI 856 before the trailer’s in-yard date and time


$0.75 per carton with a $100 minimum for ASN and barcode defects, as of 2025 ([2025 Target Compliance Changes](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/articles/2025-target-compliance-changes) )


Partners Online


Walmart


Apply through Walmart’s supplier portal, sign agreements, then gain Retail Link access, as of March 2026


ASN arrives before trailer gate-in and passes validation ([Walmart’s ASN validation process](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/articles/what-is-an-asn-walmart-validation-process) )


Flat $25 per PO under its Supplier Quality Excellence Program (SQEP), as of September 2025


Retail Link, under Apps, then EDI-B2B


Amazon


Complete Amazon’s EDI onboarding and testing through Vendor Central or an EDI provider ([EDI for Amazon ASNs](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/articles/edi-for-amazon-asns) )


ASN is sent after the shipment leaves the dock and before it arrives


Tiered percentage of product cost on a rolling 4-week compliance rate, as of September 2025


Vendor Central, with ASN errors under Reports, then Operational Performance


## When Does the Compliance Clock Start?


Retailers differ on whether a new supplier tests a connection first or starts in production.


### Kroger Starts in Production


Kroger sends production[purchase orders (POs)](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/articles/what-is-a-purchase-order) to new partners in its Food and Peyton groups and conducts no PO testing with them. Vendors that accept distribution center orders but do not yet use EDI are given 90 days to comply. This is called[provisional compliance](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/articles/how-to-set-up-edi-with-kroger) .


### Retailers That Test First


Unlike the Food and Peyton groups, the Fred Meyer Non Food group starts new partners in test or parallel mode. In that mode, the paper order stays official and the EDI order is only compared against it. A vendor can be held liable if it files a test order.


[Walmart’s Drop Ship Vendor](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/articles/connecting-apps-apis-and-integrations-in-retail-link) program involves testing and certifying an EDI or XML connection before Walmart activates a seller account. Amazon also requires EDI onboarding and testing.


**Related Reading:**[How To Onboard a New Retailer](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/articles/how-to-onboard-a-new-retailer)


## What Are the ASN Requirements at Each Retailer?


Walmart, Kroger, and Target each expect the ASN before the shipment arrives, but each defines arrival differently.


### Walmart: Before Gate-In


Walmart counts an ASN as on time if it arrives before the trailer’s gate-in time and passes validation, or if every issue is corrected and resent before gate-in. An EDI 824 marked WARN means a business rule failed but Walmart can still use the data, whereas ERROR means Walmart rejected it.


### Kroger: Before Receipt


As with Walmart, Kroger ties timing to a physical event, but the event is receipt of the product rather than arrival at the gate. The ASN must reflect the contents of the shipment, and Kroger holds the vendor liable for a return or penalty when problems in its content or timing delay receipt.


### Target: Before the In-Yard Time


Target requires an error-free EDI 856 before the trailer’s in-yard date and time. Its ASN Accuracy metric adds two checks. Shipment Accuracy looks at the format and segment of the bill of lading number. Item Accuracy compares item attributes such as case pack and barcode against the purchase order.


**Related Reading:**[Compare and Contrast: ASNs at Walmart vs. Amazon](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/articles/compare-and-contrast-asns-at-walmart-vs-amazon)


## How Do Retailers Price EDI Violations?


EDI violations are priced by different factors depending on the retailer. It's important to understand how each retailer penalizes for inaccurate data.


### Kroger: A Percentage With a Floor


After the 90-day window for distribution center purchase orders, Kroger deducts 1% of the total invoice amount or $250, whichever is greater. A vendor in EDI production that sends a paper invoice could incur the same charge per transaction, according to the terms.


### Target: A Per-Carton Rate


Target’s 2025 Perfect Order Program priced ASN availability, ASN accuracy, and physical barcode accuracy at $0.75 per carton, with a $100 minimum. Target’s[2026 policy](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/articles/target-compliance-policy-a-credit-score-for-suppliers) took effect May 3 and added Physical Casepack Accuracy and an Item Attribute Audit. Current rates should be checked in the policy on Partners Online.


### Walmart and Amazon: What the Sources Show


An SPS comparison of Walmart and Amazon ASNs from September 2025 lists a flat $25 fine per PO for Walmart under SQEP. It lists a tiered percentage of product cost for Amazon, based on a rolling 4-week compliance rate. Because this information does not come directly from the retailers, it is helpful to double-check the details.


Walmart said its May 2024 ASN rule changes would not bring new SQEP charges, though the SPS article on them notes that Walmart sets a standard, tracks compliance, and then levies fines.


**Related Reading:**[Retailer Deductions in Q4: How Walmart and Kroger Compare](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/articles/retailer-deductions-in-q4-how-walmart-and-kroger-compare)


## Can One Retailer Mean Several Rulebooks?


Yes, because Kroger’s EDI portal has ten requirement sections, including ones for Kroger/Peyton’s, Fred Meyer, and Harris Teeter. The SPS Kroger article adds that vendors need a separate EDI connection for Fred Meyer and for Harris Teeter.


The Kroger/Peyton[requirements page](https://edi.kroger.com/EDIPortal/EDIGuideAndReq_Kroger.html) lists the 850 and the 875 as purchase order documents. It lists the 810 and the 880 as invoice documents. Programs split rulebooks as well. Walmart runs a first-party (1P) relationship, a Marketplace model, and a Drop Ship Vendor program, and Target expects dropship vendors to follow its dropship standards.


**Related Reading:**[Finding the Right Purchase Order: EDI 850 vs. EDI 875](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/articles/finding-the-right-purchase-order-edi-850-vs-edi-875)


## Where Do Retailer EDI Requirements Live?


The rulebooks sit in these places:


-


**Kroger** : The EDI portal at edi.kroger.com is public and holds the terms, the requirements, and the new partner form.


-


**Walmart** : Once you are signed into Retail Link, the ASN 824 Resolution Guide sits under Apps, then EDI-B2B.


-


**Target** : The Supplier Performance Management Compliance Policy and related documents sit in Partners Online.


-


**Amazon** : ASN errors appear in Vendor Central under Reports, then Operational Performance.


## Frequently Asked Questions


### Is EDI compliance the same at every retailer?


No, because retailers share many documents. Each one still sets its own onboarding path, ASN timing, and penalty formula.


### Do these penalties apply to every vendor?


A penalty does not apply automatically. What a supplier owes depends on its vendor agreement and the retailer’s current policy.


### Where can a supplier find a retailer’s vendor compliance requirements?


Kroger publishes its rules on a public portal, while Walmart and Target keep theirs in Retail Link and Partners Online.


## Ready To Track Every Retailer’s Rules?


Retailers each set their own formats, timelines, and packing rules.[SPS Fulfillment / EDI](https://www.spscommerce.com/products/fulfillment/edi/) keeps each retailer’s requirements in its network, so suppliers do not have to track every rule set alone.
